6	\subsection{SmolVLA: Cliff-Edge Under All Pruning Methods}
7	\label{sec:smolvla_results}
8	
9	The SmolVLA baseline (bypass mode, all 128 vision tokens) achieves 44.8\% SR (224/500, CI [40.5\%, 49.2\%]).\footnote{The official SmolVLA result is 87.3\% SR with batch size 64 on 8 GPUs. Our reproduction uses a smaller batch due to compute constraints.} Table~\ref{tab:smolvla_ablation} reports the full ablation. Every pruning configuration produces 0\% SR (Wilson CI upper bounds $\leq$0.80\%). Three observations make this striking: (1)~\textbf{Scoring-independent}: random selection performs identically to learned ACIS scoring. (2)~\textbf{Ratio-independent}: retaining 95\% of tokens ($k{=}0.95$, removing only 7 of 128) causes the same failure as retaining 50\%. (3)~\textbf{Mechanism-independent}: zero-masking, true removal, and token merging all produce 0\% SR.

5	\label{sec:pixel_shuffle}
6	
7	The divergence between SmolVLA and OpenVLA co-occurs with differences in their vision connectors. SmolVLA's pixel-shuffle applies $4 \times 4$ spatial folding, so each of its 128 tokens encodes 16 patches via channel concatenation. Removing any token eliminates an entire receptive field with no redundancy from neighbors (Figure~\ref{fig:pixel_shuffle}). Because the folding is fixed and non-learned, no downstream layer can recover discarded information. OpenVLA's MLP projector maps each patch independently: removing one of 256 tokens discards $\sim$1/256 of the visual field, a localized loss that self-attention layers can partially compensate. At $k{=}0.50$, OpenVLA retains 37.4\% SR against a 74.0\% baseline; SmolVLA collapses to 0\% even at $k{=}0.95$.

10	\paragraph{Vision connectors.}
11	Per-patch MLP projectors~\cite{liu2023llava,kim2024openvla} preserve per-token granularity. Cross-attention connectors (Q-Former~\cite{li2023blip2}, Perceiver~\cite{alayrac2022flamingo,jaegle2021perceiver}, RoboFlamingo~\cite{li2024roboflamingo}) compress to learned queries at the architectural level. Pixel-shuffle connectors~\cite{shi2016subpixel,shukor2025smolvla,chen2024internvl} fold patches via channel concatenation, achieving training-time compression but creating inter-token dependencies; compact VLAs such as TinyVLA~\cite{wen2024tinyvla} adopt similar efficient connectors to reduce token counts. Our analysis links this taxonomy to inference-time compressibility and shows that cross-attention re-encoding can overcome the failure mode of deletion on pixel-shuffle architectures.
12	
13	\paragraph{VLA token compression.}
14	Recent concurrent works achieve efficient token compression on MLP-projector VLAs. Compressor-VLA~\cite{gao2025compressorvla} uses instruction-guided cross-attention compression on OpenVLA-OFT~\cite{kim2025openoft}. SpecPrune-VLA~\cite{wang2025specprunevla} applies action-aware self-speculative pruning to OpenVLA with real-robot validation. LightVLA~\cite{jiang2026lightvla} introduces differentiable token pruning for VLA efficiency. ``See What Matters''~\cite{feng2026seewhatmatters} proposes grid-based continuous resampling on $\pi_0$ and SmolVLA, focusing on the discrete-versus-continuous sampling paradigm rather than connector-dependent failure modes. SparseVLM~\cite{zhang2025sparsevlm} and SparseVILA~\cite{khaki2025sparsevila} explore token sparsification in VLMs, and ``Don't Run with Scissors''~\cite{jabbour2025dontrun} examines weight pruning fragility in VLAs. All compression methods above operate on MLP-projector architectures or evaluate pruning without diagnosing connector-dependent failure modes. Our work is complementary: we identify why deletion-based approaches catastrophically fail on pixe
…[truncated 105 chars]

9	Four lines of evidence favor the connector-level explanation. First, the official SmolVLA checkpoint (59.2\% SR baseline) exhibits the same cliff-edge under 50\% random pruning (0/500, 0.0\% SR), ruling out the possibility that our fine-tuned model's lower baseline (44.8\%) reflects undertrained weights that are unusually fragile. Second, SmolVLA collapses at $k = 0.95$, where only 7 of 128 tokens (5.5\%) are removed. A capacity-limited model that can solve the task with all tokens should not fail catastrophically when 95\% of the input is preserved; the perturbation is too small relative to the model's demonstrated capability. Third, the attention entropy ratio difference (0.95 vs.\ 0.64) is an architectural measurement, not a capacity measurement. SmolVLA's near-uniform attention distribution reflects the pixel-shuffle connector's output structure: because each token encodes 16 patches via channel concatenation, the resulting tokens are uniformly information-dense, and the downstream LLM has no basis for developing selective attention. OpenVLA's sharply non-uniform attention in deep layers reflects the MLP projector's preservation of per-patch granularity, which allows the model to learn which spatial locations carry task-relevant information. Fourth, the pixel-shuffle operation itself provides a mechanistic explanation: $4 \times 4$ spatial folding creates tokens whose meaning depends on the complete $4 \times 4$ grid, and removing any token eliminates an entire receptive field with no redundancy in the remaining tokens. The MLP projector, by contrast, produces tokens with overlapping receptive fields (inherited from the ViT encoder's patch-level self-attention), providing natural redundancy.
10

…[truncated 920 chars]

31	The primary computational benefit at this model scale is memory, not latency. Reducing from 128 to 32 vision tokens shrinks the KV-cache footprint for the vision portion by 75\%, a meaningful reduction for deployment on memory-constrained robotic hardware. For larger VLA models (7B+ parameters), where self-attention cost scales quadratically with sequence length and vision tokens constitute a larger fraction of total compute, the same 75\% token reduction would yield substantially larger latency gains. Whether the training cost is justified depends on the deployment context: for a VLA deployed across many tasks, the one-time 100K-step training cost is amortized over the deployment lifetime, while for rapid prototyping the retraining requirement is a barrier. Smart Compress is not a drop-in post-hoc optimization but a trained architectural component whose inference benefits scale with the model it serves.
32	
33	The $M = 128$ passthrough control (59.8\% SR) resolves the capacity-vs-compression question. Because $M = 128$ achieves performance statistically indistinguishable from $M = 32$ and $M = 64$ (both 61.6\%), the $\sim$15-point gain over baseline originates from the cross-attention re-encoding itself, not from compression. The 22.2M-parameter module transforms pixel-shuffle tokens into representations that the downstream LLM processes more effectively, regardless of output token count. A simple capacity explanation is also insufficient: the compressor adds 22.2M parameters (4.9\% of the 451.5M base model), while the expert action head trained in both conditions contains 99.9M parameters. If raw parameter count were the driver, the action head's capacity would already dominate; the gain instead reflects the compressor's architectural role in re-encoding spatially entangled tokens. Token reduction from 128 to 32 is then achieved at no performance cost, making compression a deployment optimization (75\% KV-cache reduction, 6\% latency gain) layered on top of the
